title: Reply thread, older request for another booking quoted below
why: The newest message asks for the check and both documents are attached; the quoted request is history.

title: Forwarded by a colleague
why: The colleague forwards the customer's request unchanged, with both documents.

title: Request only after a long forwarded header and disclaimer
why: The ask sits past the first 1,500 characters; the attachments still say what the email is for.

title: One-line body
why: SI and draft BL attached and the subject says to confirm the documents.

title: Body in Malay
why: Asks to check the attached SI and draft BL, in Malay.

title: Body in Chinese
why: Asks to check the attached SI and draft BL, in Chinese.

title: Signature logos attached next to the SI and BL
why: image001.png and image002.png are the sender's signature, not documents.

title: Revised draft BL attached next to the first draft
why: The revised BL fixes the consignee; the check is against the latest draft.
known_gap: The service takes the first file with _BL. in its name, so the first draft is compared and the revised one is ignored: a false mismatch.

title: Two shipments in one email, the second BL wrong
why: One result cannot say both pairs are fine when the second weight differs; a person must look.
known_gap: Only the first SI and BL pair is read. The second pair, with the wrong weight, is never compared and the email shows OK: a missed defect.

title: Amendment request, no documents
why: Asks to change the shipping instruction; there is nothing to compare.
category_gap: Qwen says BL_COMPARISON: the prompt rule that a request to send the draft BL is a comparison wins over the amendment. It still reaches a person as a missing attachment, but the amendment itself is not what they are shown.

title: The same email sent again
why: A resend must give the same answer as the first time (edge_a4).

title: Out-of-office reply quoting a BL email
why: An automatic reply asks for nothing.
category_gap: Qwen says BL_COMPARISON from the quoted subject and text, so an auto-reply becomes a missing-attachment task for staff.

title: Phishing dressed as a draft BL
why: An unknown portal asks for a click and a sign-in to 'view' a BL; nothing is attached.
category_gap: Qwen says BL_COMPARISON: a phishing link asking for an email password is shown to staff as a genuine BL task instead of spam.

title: Invoice query quoting a BL number
why: The BL number is a reference; the question is about charges.

title: Consignee differs only in case and spacing
why: Case and spaces are formatting (rules: collapse whitespace, uppercase).
known_gap: clean_entity treats two spaces as the start of the address and cuts the name there, so 'Moorim  SP Co., Ltd' becomes MOORIM: a false mismatch.

title: CO., LTD against COMPANY LIMITED
why: On a title document the legal name as written is the identity; a person confirms (rules: suffix is identity).

title: M/S in front of the consignee
why: Exact compare by the rules; a person confirms whether M/S is only a courtesy.

title: Two spaces inside two different names
why: MOORIM SP and MOORIM PAPER are different companies, however many spaces the template puts in.
known_gap: Same cause as edge_b1a the other way round: both names are cut to MOORIM and match, so a different company passes as OK: a missed defect.

title: Port with a country code against the locode
why: SHANGHAI, CN and SHANGHAI (CNSHA) are the same port.

title: Weight with decimals and KGS
why: 21,577.00 KGS and 21,577 KG are the same weight.

title: Weight in tonnes
Weight with a European decimal comma
why: 21.577,00 KG is 21,577 kg written the European way.
known_gap: The weight is read as 21.577 kg instead of 21,577 kg: a false mismatch.

title: Container count written out
why: ONE (1) X 40' HIGH CUBE is 1 x 40'HC.

title: TO ORDER against TO THE ORDER OF a bank
why: A bank-order consignee is a different party from a plain order consignee.

title: Notify party SAME AS CONSIGNEE against the name
why: Same party in meaning, different instruction on the BL; a person confirms.

title: One-letter defect: I against lowercase l
why: MOORlM is a typo that looks right on screen; it must be caught.

title: Consignee name split across two lines
why: The name wraps onto the next line in the SI; it is the same name.
known_gap: The reader keeps only the first line of a value, so a name wrapped onto the next line is cut to MOORIM SP: a false mismatch.

title: File named SI is actually a BL
why: The filename lies; the document header decides (rules: verify document type first).

title: Empty SI file
why: An empty file cannot be checked.

title: Password-protected PDF
why: The file will not open without the password.

title: SI sent as a photo
why: A phone photo of the SI has no text to read.
